title: Variable Reassignment
prompt:
Reassign a value to a variable and understand the implications
Sample Input: x = 10, x = 20
Sample Output: 20
answer:
Sure, I'd be happy to help with that! The sample input you provided indicates that the variable 'x' has been assigned two different values, '10' and '20'. When you reassign a value to a variable, it effectively replaces the previous value with the new one. Here's how you can understand the implications:

In the first line of the sample input, 'x = 10', the variable 'x' is assigned the value '10'. This means that if you were to print the value of 'x' at this point, it would be '10'.

In the second line of the sample input, 'x = 20', the variable 'x' is reassigned to the value '20'. This means that the previous value of 'x' (which was '10') is now replaced by '20'. Therefore, if you were to print the value of 'x' again after this reassignment, it would be '20'.

To summarize, reassigning a value to a variable effectively replaces the previous value with the new one. In the given sample input, 'x = 10' and 'x = 20', the variable 'x' has been assigned two different values, '10' and '20', respectively.
